approach.method_basis: The Parent keeps a persistent forest of molecular transformation paths rooted in the supplied initial molecules. Actual terminal scores update each traversed occurrence’s visit count, total return and best completed return; pending proposals have a separate count. At both the initial-root choice and deeper choices, a molecular-similarity kernel averages the visited siblings’ best returns with visit-count weights, then adds the inherited exploration bonus. The tree expands under pending-aware widening and makes two successful rollout transitions before purchasing an eligible terminal. It has no active global surrogate or scored-population breeder.
approach.novelty: Root-only peak removal restores the already computed shared mean when choosing among the supplied initial roots, while deeper choices retain peak exploitation. This tests whether remembered root peaks concentrate follow-up without useful endpoint contribution. The earlier mean-to-peak intervention changed both levels together; no evaluated same-Parent child in this brief isolates the root consumer. The separate frontier experiment changes rollout continuation, which this intervention preserves.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-5cc901d1a9e3 concentrates follow-up on historical peaks and leaves the root-specific contribution unidentified. Its completed Search mean is 0.32678476606627965 (population SD 0.04159141942323312), +0.015171463365010665 versus mean-at-both-levels n-4e4e248bd6bd, but the paired seed changes are +0.116426470099259, -0.0038346592133600144 and -0.06707742079086698. Its difference from formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de is -0.2802455501448513. All three actual summary.json/run.log pairs report successful completion. Independent chronological replay of every frozen Search cell, joined to all 4350 actual optimizer purchases, reproduces 3717/4380 root and 3305/7311 deeper best-versus-mean choice changes with zero checked selector or final N/W/M/pending discrepancies. Only 137/150 supplied roots receive optimizer follow-up; 10644/13051 nonroot occurrences remain singletons and 2280 receive repeated feedback. Mean within-cell root purchase HHI is 0.2716829171621086; gain HHI is 0.711714391604323 across the 13 positive-gain cells, with two zero-gain cells explicitly undefined. One receipt supplies 0.23560362766312273 of total incumbent gain. The inherited tree n-eca1b7eb5895 and both-level mean ancestor do not isolate root peak contribution. These data support the frozen root-only removal, not a revival of the original whole-controller conversion prediction. Exact per-cell audits and their underlying log/trajectory/summary/run files are enumerated and hashed in policy/scratch/r0053-01-improve-L01-plan/audit-evidence-manifest.json; the source audit is policy/scratch/r0053-01-improve-L01-plan/audit.py. Parent analysis is nodes/n-5cc901d1a9e3/analysis.json.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse exactly the frozen Search Policy Root-only peak-return contribution isolation entry and its recorded review. No new search query was issued for this plan; the primary SameGame PDF was reopened and its selection, backup and final-move sections checked. It does not establish the proposed molecular contribution. Internal Parent evidence supports one directly implementable categorical removal while preserving deeper peak use, two-transition rollouts and pending-aware widening; empty adoptions are intentional.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The frozen root-only removal is justified by completed Parent selector exposure, narrowed initial-root follow-up and the missing isolated contribution comparison. No new literature-derived component is introduced. The already present maximum ledger and molecular kernel are inherited code, not fresh adoptions. Both-level mean and peak outcomes plus passive choice replay do not price removal of only the root consumer.

hypothesis: Remove only the best-return exploitation consumer at virtual parent 0. For the identical eligible sibling rows retain K_ij, D_i=sum_j K_ij*N_j, S_i=sum_j K_ij*W_j, P_i=sum_j K_ij*O_j and B_i=sum_{j:N_j>0} K_ij*N_j*M_j. At _choose(parent_id=0), use S_i/D_i as exploitation when D_i>0, otherwise the inherited neutral 0.5. At every parent_id!=0 continue to use B_i/D_i with the same neutral rule. Both levels retain the identical bonus 0.5*sqrt(2*log(max(2,N_parent+O_parent))/(D_i+P_i)), D_i+P_i==0 priority and earliest-occurrence tie. Preserve all accepted-only maximum ledgers and all-return N/W/Q, independent O, initial normalization, route-local receipt identity and alias isolation. Reducing the influence of isolated root maxima should broaden initial-root follow-up and reduce allocation/gain concentration while retaining deeper peak exploitation. This is a conditional component removal; no additional arm or alternative adaptive trajectory is introduced.

finding_summary.headline: Root coverage broadened and mean score rose, but gain concentration remained mixed
finding_summary.insights: On this complete finite panel, retaining peak exploitation at the root has negative conditional endpoint contribution when deeper peak exploitation is retained. That answers the component question, but it does not show that broader allocation caused the score gain: one docking seed supplies the dominant improvement, receipt concentration increases, and later purchases yield less gain. The inconclusive mechanism verdict concerns that mixed explanatory chain; execution succeeded, the score improved, and the registered joint coverage/concentration falsifier did not trigger. This settles neither the value of deeper peak selection nor the tree approach as a whole. The remaining method limitation is now clearer: merely reaching every initial root does not produce sustained productive refinement. Of 13,044 nonroot occurrences, 10,605 received only one return; terminals using earlier-announcement prefix feedback barely changed, from 3,156 to 3,130 of 4,350. Molecular evidence shows broad ring and scaffold exploration, with fewer tiny fragments but more products above fifty heavy atoms (461 versus 401), reactive motifs and no assigned tetrahedral stereochemistry. The strong docking tail includes amine-rich structures already accessible to the generator, while most sampled molecules remain weak. These observations support investigating a proposal operator that preserves useful cores and functional-group roles, or a search scheme that obtains more informative repeated feedback on promising prefixes. They do not establish a missing pharmacophore, a universal size cutoff, or a benefit from retuning the same root statistic.
finding_summary.results: The intended selector change ran correctly in all 15 task/seed cells: 3,207 of 4,358 root decisions changed, with no arithmetic or receipt-accounting discrepancies and deeper peak selection preserved. All 150 supplied roots received optimizer follow-up, up from 137, and root purchase concentration fell from 0.27168 to 0.16563. Within the 12 cells where both runs gained, root gain concentration also fell, from 0.68769 to 0.56379. But the largest receipt accounted for 25.51% of total gain versus 23.56%, and the largest task/seed cell accounted for 38.33% versus 25.92%. Full gain rose from 1.77439 to 2.23597 while second-half gain fell from 1.07389 to 0.54762. Thus the broader-allocation result is established, but the full gain-deconcentration explanation remains mixed. Mean endpoint score rose from 0.32678 to 0.35756, a paired gain of 0.03077 above the supplied 0.002 scale; seed changes were -0.05647, +0.02191 and +0.12688. The mean remains 0.24947 below the formal Anchor.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aryl/heterocycle chemistry with useful compact examples, but persistent fragments, oversized hybrids and reactive motifs
molecular.overall_character: Node n-7532fea6b682 produces aryl and heteroaryl assemblies, pyrazoline/thioamide relatives, methoxyindoles, carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles, acetal-rich polycycles, amines, halogenated fragments and large hybrids. This is broad constitutional exploration, not absence of rings or aromatic chemistry: digest ring-closure rates are 0.7954-0.8621 and aromatic-presence rates 0.5517-0.7402 across the tasks; these are string-level molecule-presence rates, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Each task has 900 observed records, including 870 accepted optimizer records across Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. The complete Child and all published code-Parent n-5cc901d1a9e3 trajectories were read; context.comparison independently says child_complete=true and paired_complete=true. No task or Parent path is missing; no Anchor molecular comparison is asserted. All chemistry counts concern accepted records, not unobserved rejected/internal proposals. RDKit 2023.09.6 readings of the 4350 accepted optimizer records find 502 below six heavy atoms and 461 above fifty, compared with 609 and 401 for the Parent. Thus fewer tiny fragments coexist with more oversized products; this is not uniformly improved molecular size. Nonempty Murcko scaffolds occur in 3606 Child records versus 3409 Parent records. Per-cell distinct nonempty typed/generic scaffold counts are preserved in the audits and are not added across cells. Common medicinal motifs and many moderate-sized graphs justify moderate drug-likeness, but arbitrary ring closures, unstable-looking linkages and very large assemblies make overall synthetic plausibility questionable. A graph that parses is not a validated synthesis or a stable compound. The explicit single-bond N/O/S-to-halogen pattern occurs in 339 Child records versus 433 Parent records; O-O bonds occur in 198 versus 246. These overlapping structural flags are not experimental reactivity measurements. Unacylated aliphatic amine motifs are present in 1035 Child records versus 904 Parent records, so an inability to generate basic-amine-like centres would be an incorrect diagnosis. The defined SMARTS identifies connectivity, not pKa or protonation. No Child record has assigned tetrahedral stereochemistry; RDKit detects unassigned centres in 2783 optimizer records. The frozen authority is policy/requests/r0053-01-improve-L01-molecular-assess-07fe62b678ad1d0f.json. policy/scratch/r0053-01-improve-L01-molecular/evidence-manifest.json lists each actual input and hash, and summary.json in that same scratch location holds derived totals. Active Child trajectories remain at the exact trusted citation_trajectory_paths outside the run directory; the audits explicitly preserve that authorized staging provenance instead of inventing future archive sources. Parent input files are published run-relative Search trajectories. These output associations establish neither mechanism activation nor contribution of the root selector; all transferable gaps below originate in this complete Search panel under the frozen profile and remain conditional on these molecules.

per_task.generated_character: Predominantly aryl pyrazoline/thioamide and fused heteroaryl chemistry, mixed with phenols, ethers, esters and amides. The best examples have 23, 24 or 25 heavy atoms, whereas per-seed optimizer medians are 25, 23 and 24 and the full task spans 1-100 heavy atoms. There are 95 accepted fragments below six heavy atoms and 59 products above fifty. The digest ring-closure/aromatic-presence rates are 0.8425/0.6724. The leading dimethylthiourea-like pyrazoline contains a phenyl group and an unusual oxygen-bridged aryl ring; the high quinazoline-containing fluoroacetamide also has a four-membered oxygen-containing ring. Both are chemically less ordinary than their recognizable aromatic and amide pieces suggest. Cell-level provenance and derived descriptors: policy/scratch/r0053-01-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json, policy/scratch/r0053-01-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-1-zaleplon_mpo.json, policy/scratch/r0053-01-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-2-zaleplon_mpo.json.
liabilities: The leading structures include unusual four-membered oxygen-containing ring closures, and no tetrahedral configuration is specified.

Upper-tail examples also include O-Cl and O-F substituents; the final excerpt includes an O-O-containing large hybrid. A favorable scalar score does not validate these groups as stable medicinal chemistry.
missing_features: Consistent retention of the compact aromatic-plus-polar architecture seen in the upper tail is missing from many later purchases; very small fragments and large acetal/aryl recombinations remain present.
The high-scoring heterocyclic motifs are not accompanied by a demonstrated set of comparably scoring, less strained analogues. The evidence does not reveal a specific missing target pharmacophore.

The compact aryl pyrazoline carrying a methoxycarbonyl-thiocarbonyl substituent scores 0.3697260049130546; the dimethylthiourea-like pyrazoline scores 0.4360308581149081, and the fused quinazoline/fluoroacetamide scores 0.4291508451801343. The data do not establish any specific omitted recognition group. A credible compact scaffold-change series with preserved attachment geometry is an unresolved capability, not a known objective answer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-7532fea6b682, complete frozen Search panel, with published n-5cc901d1a9e3 as baseline: 502 of 4350 accepted optimizer records have fewer than six heavy atoms and 461 exceed fifty, versus Parent 609 and 401. Compact aromatic/heterocyclic upper-tail examples coexist with late fragments and concatenated aryl/acetal products. Some favorable molecules are large, so the observations do not justify a universal hard size cutoff.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful molecular cores are not consistently preserved through size-controlled, limited structural changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic proposal system could preserve an accepted core and its attachment context while making bounded local changes or deleting peripheral groups. Let current-session feedback determine which cores and sizes remain useful. This is a chemically motivated follow-up capability, not attribution to the changed selector or evidence that a fixed size filter will improve score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-7532fea6b682 under the frozen Search conditions: 339 accepted records contain a single N/O/S-halogen bond and 198 an O-O bond; the corresponding Parent counts are 433 and 246. These flags therefore persist despite being less frequent. Several upper-tail structures also contain unusual four-membered ring arrangements or reactive carbonyl/thiol groups. Counts overlap and are structural flags, not measured instability.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically credible alternatives to reactive bonds and strained ring closures are not systematically represented around the favorable structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Develop context-aware bond and ring transformations that can replace an alerted linkage while preserving the neighboring core and functional geometry, and compare their actual current-session returns. Do not interpret valid SMILES or a high score as synthetic validation, and do not assume blanket exclusion of every alert is supported.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The current complete Search output contains 1035 accepted records matching the specified unacylated aliphatic-amine connectivity pattern, compared with 904 in the Parent; basic-amine-like groups are available. Favorable examples include arylalkyl amines, but the stream also replaces nitrogen roles with acylated, sulfonylated, N-N or N-halogen arrangements. These are molecular associations in n-7532fea6b682, with counterexamples and seed dependence, not a universal preferred group.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group role is not consistently preserved when useful ring and linker arrangements are varied.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Permit local variation of ring/linker geometry while maintaining a chosen accepted molecule's donor/acceptor and amine-versus-amide roles, as well as deliberate isolated changes to those roles. Selection must use only the current session's observations; neither task identity nor a fixed target pharmacophore should enter generation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All five digest stereocentre-text rates are zero. RDKit reads zero optimizer molecules with assigned tetrahedral centres and 2783 with unassigned centres in the complete 4350-record Child Search output, including favorable fused-ring and arylalkyl-amine examples. This is a representation and exploration gap; these trajectories contain no measured stereoisomer contrast that establishes a score benefit.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated constitutional diversity has no corresponding assigned tetrahedral stereochemical diversity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could retain valid stereochemical information and offer local stereoisomer changes when an accepted graph has stereogenic centres, under the same canonical identity and budget rules. Whether that capability helps requires new same-session observations; no preferred configuration is inferred here.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Persistent route-local molecular prefix tree with fixed ten supplied initial roots, canonical aliases without cross-occurrence credit, accepted-only archive donors and bounded de novo graph proposals.
Count-Tanimoto sibling sharing of completed density D, all-return sum S and pending density P; root shared mean S/D and retained deeper count-weighted peak B/D.
Exact N/W/Q and accepted-only M with earliest attaining receipt; pending O affects exploration only; same exploration coefficient, neutral value, unvisited priority and earliest-occurrence tie.
Raw N+O square-root widening, maximum graph depth 12, normal and reserve occurrence caps, two successful rollout transitions and inherited crossover finishing gate.

Inherited graph crossover/mutation probabilities, donor snapshots, arctangent normalization, terminal-on-route novelty checks, pending reconciliation and bounded fallbacks; no active global GP, stall mask or greedy breeder.
